minutes.headline: PACC voted unanimously to request a transfer from new equipment capital to videographer payroll, pending Town Manager approval.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a manager's report showing record programming had nearly exhausted the videographer payroll line. After long debate over sources and size, it voted to request a line item transfer from capital to payroll. It also reviewed minutes, discussed H74 advocacy, the Enterprise fund and interest, and an Owl camera idea.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the tech crew for a workaround during a baseball broadcast when the TriCaster failed, and suggested a live call-in telethon fundraiser modelled on the Dollars for Scholars telethon at another town's cable studio.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of the previous meeting as amended.

budget_items.what_was_said: Heavy programming and long meetings have nearly depleted the payroll line for videographers, so the manager asked for a line item transfer.
The videography budget was increased for next year but cannot be changed now since it has been through the finance committee and goes to town meeting in May.
Capital is the only line with enough money, but it covers catastrophic failure such as the TriCaster; some was already moved to equipment maintenance and supplies.
Members discussed moving in smaller monthly amounts versus one transfer; the town accountant prefers one transfer. A compromise of a first tranche was settled with a review in June.
A member asked whether the manager's own salary line has leftover money that could cover part of the need; the manager said some remains for three months and it will be revisited.
A resident noted a spreadsheet discrepancy; the chair said the presentation total, operations plus capital, is the correct one.
The ending balance is off by an amount that the finance director could not explain yet; the manager keeps looking.
Return of indirect costs taken in FY23 remains unresolved, so reported balances are lower than they should be.

The quarterly Enterprise fund statement is not yet received; no interest has been received since December and a portion is uninvested. Interest and franchise fees are operating income; bond interest is held for the new studio.
The cost of an Owl video conferencing device was discussed and the manager was asked to look into feasibility of using the town's existing one.
A resident described a telethon that raised money for scholarships as a model for a small start-up call-in program.

what_happened.line: The Public Access Cable Committee voted unanimously to request a line item transfer from new equipment capital to videographer payroll, pending Town Manager approval.
The manager reported that heavy programming and long meetings had nearly used up the videographer payroll line, which prompted the request.
Members settled on a first tranche now, with the need for more to be reviewed at the June meeting, rather than one full transfer.
The manager was asked to look into getting or taking over an Owl camera for recording town committee meetings; no purchase was decided.
The committee agreed a letter supporting H74 will be finished and sent to the legislator by the April 8 deadline.

why_it_matters: Cable access budgets are small, and capital set aside for equipment failure was drawn on to keep videographers paid for meeting coverage that residents watch.
The videography budget was raised for next year but is already past the Finance Committee, so it goes to Town Meeting in May as is; the current-year gap was handled by a transfer instead.
watch_next: Town Manager approval of the requested transfer, and the June review of whether more is needed.
Next committee meeting on May 6; the H74 letter is due by April 8.
